## A

### Access control list

the list of users and groups permitted to access a resource, and with what rights (ACL). *See [Ch 17](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch17-unstructured-data-processing.md).*

### ACID

atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability: the guarantees that make database transactions safe. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### ACL propagation

carrying a source document's permissions onto every derived chunk, vector and cached answer. *See [Ch 17](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch17-unstructured-data-processing.md).*

### Acquihire

a deal whose main purpose is hiring a team rather than buying a business or its products. *See [Ch 20](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch20-training-data-supply-chain.md).*

### Active metadata

Metadata that triggers actions such as alerts, policy changes or agent context instead of only being displayed in a catalog portal. *See [Ch 33](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch33-governance-catalog-security-companies.md).*

### ADBC

Arrow Database Connectivity, a database client API that returns results as Arrow batches, a columnar counterpart to JDBC/ODBC. *See [Ch 06](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch06-file-formats.md).*

### Agent Bricks

Databricks' tooling to build, evaluate and automatically optimise AI agents on governed enterprise data. *See [Ch 25](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch25-databricks.md).*

### Agent memory

information an AI agent stores outside its context window and recalls in later steps or sessions. *See [Ch 22](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch22-agents-and-data.md).*

### Agent2Agent protocol

an open protocol (A2A), launched by Google in 2025 and now at the Linux Foundation, that lets AI agents delegate tasks to other agents. *See [Ch 22](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch22-agents-and-data.md).*

### Agentforce

Salesforce's AI agent platform, launched in 2024 and priced per conversation and later per action. *See [Ch 34](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch34-application-giants-data-platforms.md).*

### Agentic AI Foundation

the Linux Foundation directed fund, co-founded by Anthropic, Block and OpenAI, that has governed MCP since December 2025. *See [Ch 22](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch22-agents-and-data.md).*

### Agentic identity

treating an AI agent as a distinct, auditable principal whose rights never exceed those of the user it serves. *See [Ch 22](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch22-agents-and-data.md).*

### Agentic RAG

Retrieval exposed as a tool that an AI agent calls repeatedly, refining queries and switching sources until it has enough evidence. *See [Ch 19](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch19-retrieval-architectures.md).*

### Agentless scanning

Scanning cloud data through provider APIs and snapshots without installing software on hosts, the default DSPM deployment model. *See [Ch 33](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch33-governance-catalog-security-companies.md).*

### Aggregate awareness

a query engine's ability to route a request to a smaller pre-built rollup table when that table can answer it. *See [Ch 14](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch14-semantic-layers-and-bi.md).*

### AGPL

The GNU Affero General Public License, an OSI-approved copyleft licence whose source-sharing duty also applies when software is offered over a network. *See [Ch 29](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch29-operational-database-vendors.md).*

### AI agent

A model-driven program that plans and calls tools, including data queries, to complete a task. *See [Ch 01](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch01-data-stack-map.md).*

### AI gateway

a proxy in front of multiple model providers that handles routing, failover, credentials, rate limits, caching and spend caps. *See [Ch 21](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch21-ml-platforms-feature-stores-llmops.md).*

### All-stock merger

A combination in which one company's shareholders receive the other's shares, so no cash price or new valuation is set. *See [Ch 30](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch30-data-movement-streaming-companies.md).*

### Analytics engineering

The discipline of applying software practices (version control, code review, CI, tests) to SQL data transformation. *See [Ch 12](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch12-transformation-and-orchestration.md).*

### Apache Arrow

A language-neutral, in-memory columnar data layout that lets tools share data without converting it. *See [Ch 06](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch06-file-formats.md).*

### Apache Avro

A row-oriented binary file and serialization format that embeds its schema and defines rules for reading data written under older schemas. *See [Ch 06](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch06-file-formats.md).*

### Apache Iceberg

An open table format created at Netflix that tracks table state through a tree of metadata and manifest files. *See [Ch 25](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch25-databricks.md).*

### Apache ORC

Optimized Row Columnar, a columnar file format created in 2013 by Hortonworks with Facebook to speed up Hive. *See [Ch 06](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch06-file-formats.md).*

### Apache Parquet

The default open columnar file format for analytics, created by Twitter and Cloudera in 2013 using Dremel's nested-data encoding. *See [Ch 06](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch06-file-formats.md).*

### Apache Polaris

An open-source Iceberg REST catalog donated by Snowflake in 2024 that became an Apache top-level project in 2026. *See [Ch 27](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch27-databricks-vs-snowflake.md).*

### Apache Ranger

an open-source framework for defining and enforcing data access policies across Hadoop-era platforms such as Hive, HDFS and Kafka. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

### Apache Spark

A distributed data-processing engine created at UC Berkeley's AMPLab and the foundation of Databricks. *See [Ch 25](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch25-databricks.md).*

### Apache XTable

an incubating Apache project that translates table metadata between Iceberg, Delta Lake and Hudi without copying data files. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Append-only log

An ordered sequence of records that is only ever appended to, with readers tracking their position by offset. *See [Ch 11](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch11-streaming-and-event-platforms.md).*

### Approximate nearest neighbor

Similarity search that trades a little recall for large speed gains, using indexes such as HNSW. *See [Ch 02](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch02-data-models.md).*

### ARIES

IBM's 1992 write-ahead-logging recovery algorithm with analysis, redo and undo passes. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### Arithmetic intensity

the number of operations a job performs per byte it moves; it determines whether the job is compute-bound or bandwidth-bound. *See [Ch 24](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch24-data-meets-compute-and-storage.md).*

### Arrow Flight

A gRPC-based protocol for streaming Arrow record batches between services without row-by-row serialization. *See [Ch 06](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch06-file-formats.md).*

### Atlas

MongoDB's fully managed, consumption-priced database service on AWS, Azure and Google Cloud. *See [Ch 29](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch29-operational-database-vendors.md).*

### Attribute-based access control

a model that decides access at request time from attributes of the user, the data, the action and the context. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

## B

### B-tree

a shallow, wide, sorted tree of fixed-size pages used for indexes and tables; the common B+tree variant keeps all data in leaf pages linked left to right. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### Backfill

Reprocessing historical data to fill gaps or apply corrected logic to past periods. *See [Ch 09](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch09-pipeline-patterns.md).*

### Benchmark decontamination

removing evaluation questions and answers from training data so benchmark scores are not inflated. *See [Ch 20](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch20-training-data-supply-chain.md).*

### Bi-encoder

A model that embeds queries and documents separately, so document vectors can be pre-computed and searched quickly. *See [Ch 19](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch19-retrieval-architectures.md).*

### BigQuery

Google Cloud's serverless data warehouse, descended from Google's internal Dremel engine. *See [Ch 28](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch28-hyperscaler-data-platforms.md).*

### Binary quantization

Storing one bit per vector dimension, a 32x size cut, usually followed by rescoring. *See [Ch 18](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch18-embeddings-and-vector-search.md).*

### Binlog

MySQL's binary log of committed changes, used for replication and change data capture. *See [Ch 09](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch09-pipeline-patterns.md).*

### BIRD benchmark

a text-to-SQL benchmark with large, messy databases and external-knowledge hints, with a human baseline of about 93% execution accuracy. *See [Ch 22](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch22-agents-and-data.md).*

### Bit-packing

storing integers using only the minimum number of bits their range requires. *See [Ch 05](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch05-analytical-engines.md).*

### Bitmap index

an index storing one bit-vector per distinct column value, suited to low-cardinality analytic filters. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### Bloom filter

a compact probabilistic data structure that answers "definitely not present" or "maybe present" for a key. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### BM25

The standard keyword relevance-scoring function used by Lucene, Elasticsearch and OpenSearch. *See [Ch 02](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch02-data-models.md).*

### Bring your own cloud

A deployment model (BYOC) in which a vendor's data plane runs inside the customer's own cloud account. *See [Ch 11](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch11-streaming-and-event-platforms.md).*

### Broker

A Kafka server that stores partitions and serves producer writes and consumer reads. *See [Ch 11](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch11-streaming-and-event-platforms.md).*

### Buffer pool

the database's own in-memory cache of data and index pages. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### Business catalog

a tool for people to discover, understand and trust data through search, a business glossary and stewardship workflows (e.g., Collibra, Alation, Atlan). *See [Ch 08](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch08-catalogs-and-metastores.md).*

### Business Data Cloud

SAP's data service (2025) that packages application data as semantic data products, with Databricks embedded. *See [Ch 34](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch34-application-giants-data-platforms.md).*

### Business Source License

A source-available licence (BSL) that restricts certain production uses for a set period, after which the code converts to an open-source licence. *See [Ch 29](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch29-operational-database-vendors.md).*

## C

### Cache tier

fast local storage (SSD or memory) that holds a hot working set in front of slower object storage. *See [Ch 24](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch24-data-meets-compute-and-storage.md).*

### CAGRA

NVIDIA's GPU-optimised graph vector index, part of the cuVS library. *See [Ch 18](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch18-embeddings-and-vector-search.md).*

### CAP theorem

the result that a replicated system facing a network partition must choose between consistency and availability. *See [Ch 04](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch04-distributed-databases.md).*

### Capacity-based pricing

billing for reserved processing capacity rather than for data volume moved. *See [Ch 10](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch10-ingestion-and-integration.md).*

### Cardinality estimation

predicting how many rows each step of a query plan will produce. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### Catalog federation

one catalog discovering, governing and querying tables that are registered in another catalog without copying them. *See [Ch 08](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch08-catalogs-and-metastores.md).*

### Catalog-managed table

a Delta Lake table (4.1+) whose commits are ratified by its catalog rather than by the filesystem. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Change data capture

Reading a database's transaction log to emit each committed change as an event for downstream systems. *See [Ch 01](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch01-data-stack-map.md).*

### Checkpoint

a point at which a database flushes dirty pages so crash recovery can start from there instead of the log's beginning. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### Chunk overlap

text repeated at the boundary of adjacent chunks so that context is not lost at the split. *See [Ch 17](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch17-unstructured-data-processing.md).*

### Chunking

splitting documents into retrievable units, each of which gets its own embedding. *See [Ch 17](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch17-unstructured-data-processing.md).*

### Cloud marketplace

A hyperscaler storefront where customers buy third-party software on their cloud bill. *See [Ch 28](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch28-hyperscaler-data-platforms.md).*

### Cloud repatriation

moving workloads or data from public cloud back to on-premises or private infrastructure. *See [Ch 24](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch24-data-meets-compute-and-storage.md).*

### Clustered index

a table stored as a B-tree ordered by its primary key, with full rows in the leaves (as in InnoDB). *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### Codebook

The learned set of representative sub-vectors that product quantization codes point into. *See [Ch 18](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch18-embeddings-and-vector-search.md).*

### Column chunk

The contiguous bytes of one column inside one Parquet row group, split into pages. *See [Ch 06](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch06-file-formats.md).*

### Column-level lineage

Tracing which upstream columns feed each downstream column, typically derived by parsing SQL. *See [Ch 12](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch12-transformation-and-orchestration.md).*

### Column-level security

a policy that blocks or masks specific columns depending on who is asking. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

### Columnar replica

A column-format copy of row-store data, kept current by replication, used to serve analytical reads in HTAP systems (e.g., TiFlash). *See [Ch 23](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch23-real-time-analytics-htap.md).*

### Columnar storage

storing each column's values contiguously so analytical queries read only the columns they need. *See [Ch 05](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch05-analytical-engines.md).*

### Committed spend

A multi-year contract in which a customer promises a minimum spend with a cloud provider in exchange for discounts, with any shortfall still billed. *See [Ch 28](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch28-hyperscaler-data-platforms.md).*

### Compaction

a maintenance job that rewrites many small or delete-laden files into fewer, larger, often sorted files. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Compare-and-swap

an atomic operation that updates a value only if it still equals an expected value; the primitive behind table-format commits. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Composable data stack

building data systems from shared, interchangeable components such as Arrow, Velox and DataFusion. *See [Ch 05](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch05-analytical-engines.md).*

### Compute plane

The layer where data is actually processed; in Databricks it sits in the customer's cloud account (classic) or the vendor's (serverless). *See [Ch 25](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch25-databricks.md).*

### Compute-in-memory

placing processing logic next to or inside memory so data does not have to move to a separate processor. *See [Ch 32](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch32-ai-native-data-companies.md).*

### Conditional write

an object-store write that succeeds only if a precondition holds, such as the object not already existing. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Connector

code that extracts data from one source type (SaaS API, database, file) and emits standardized records to a destination. *See [Ch 10](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch10-ingestion-and-integration.md).*

### Connector SDK

a development kit for writing custom connectors that a vendor's managed runtime hosts and meters. *See [Ch 10](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch10-ingestion-and-integration.md).*

### Consensus

a protocol by which a group of replicas agrees on a single ordered log of operations despite crashes and message delays. *See [Ch 04](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch04-distributed-databases.md).*

### Consistent hashing

placing nodes and keys on a hash ring so adding or removing a node moves only a small share of keys. *See [Ch 04](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch04-distributed-databases.md).*

### Consumer group

A set of consumers that divide a topic's partitions among themselves, with the group tracking its own committed offsets. *See [Ch 11](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch11-streaming-and-event-platforms.md).*

### Content hash

a fingerprint of a file's bytes used to detect changes and duplicates during sync. *See [Ch 17](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch17-unstructured-data-processing.md).*

### Context engineering

Choosing, on every model call, which instructions, retrieved data, tool results and history enter the model's context window. *See [Ch 16](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch16-ai-data-lifecycle.md).*

### Context precision

A retrieval metric for the share of retrieved passages that are relevant, weighted toward the top ranks. *See [Ch 19](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch19-retrieval-architectures.md).*

### Context rot

The decline in model reliability as input length grows, even on simple tasks (Chroma, 2025). *See [Ch 19](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch19-retrieval-architectures.md).*

### Contrastive learning

Training that pulls matching pairs (e.g., question and answer passage) together in vector space and pushes non-matching pairs apart. *See [Ch 18](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch18-embeddings-and-vector-search.md).*

### Control plane

The vendor-hosted services that manage, schedule and govern work, separate from where data is processed. *See [Ch 25](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch25-databricks.md).*

### Converged index

Rockset's design of storing every field in a row index, a column index and a search index at once. *See [Ch 23](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch23-real-time-analytics-htap.md).*

### Conversational analytics

natural-language question answering over governed data inside a BI tool or data platform. *See [Ch 14](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch14-semantic-layers-and-bi.md).*

### Coopetition

Competing and cooperating with the same company at the same time, as hyperscalers do with Databricks and Snowflake. *See [Ch 28](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch28-hyperscaler-data-platforms.md).*

### Copy-on-write

applying row-level changes by rewriting the affected data files in full, making writes costly and reads simple. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Cosine similarity

Similarity between two vectors measured by the angle between them; equal to the dot product for unit-length vectors. *See [Ch 18](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch18-embeddings-and-vector-search.md).*

### Covering index

an index that contains every column a query needs, so the table itself need not be read. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### Credential vending

a catalog issuing short-lived storage credentials, scoped to one table's prefix, to an engine it has authorized. *See [Ch 08](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch08-catalogs-and-metastores.md).*

### Cross-encoder

A model that reads a query and a passage together and outputs one relevance score; accurate but too slow to run over a whole corpus. *See [Ch 19](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch19-retrieval-architectures.md).*

### cuDF

the RAPIDS GPU dataframe library, whose pandas accelerator mode runs pandas code on GPUs with CPU fallback. *See [Ch 24](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch24-data-meets-compute-and-storage.md).*

### cuObject

NVIDIA libraries that move S3 object payloads over RDMA into GPU or host memory while keeping the S3 control path on HTTP. *See [Ch 24](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch24-data-meets-compute-and-storage.md).*

### Cursor field

a column such as updated_at that a connector uses to find changed records. *See [Ch 10](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch10-ingestion-and-integration.md).*

### cuVS

the RAPIDS library for building and searching vector indexes on GPUs, integrated into Faiss, Milvus and OpenSearch. *See [Ch 24](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch24-data-meets-compute-and-storage.md).*

### Cypher

Neo4j's declarative property-graph query language and the main basis for ISO GQL. *See [Ch 02](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch02-data-models.md).*

## D

### Dark data

stored data whose content and business value the organisation does not know. *See [Ch 17](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch17-unstructured-data-processing.md).*

### Data access governance

Analysing and right-sizing who can access which data, especially file shares, Microsoft 365 and SaaS content. *See [Ch 33](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch33-governance-catalog-security-companies.md).*

### Data catalog

The registry of data assets, owners, lineage and access policies that spans every layer of the stack. *See [Ch 01](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch01-data-stack-map.md).*

### Data classification

labelling data by type and sensitivity (for example, email address, card number, health data) so policies can act on it. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

### Data clean room

an environment where two or more parties analyse combined data under agreed rules without seeing each other's rows. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

### Data Cloud

Salesforce's customer-data and lakehouse layer behind Agentforce, reportedly renamed Data 360 in 2025. *See [Ch 34](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch34-application-giants-data-platforms.md).*

### Data contract

A producer-owned, enforced agreement on a dataset's schema, semantics, quality rules and SLAs. *See [Ch 12](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch12-transformation-and-orchestration.md).*

### Data curation

Extracting, filtering, deduplicating, quality-scoring and cleaning raw data into training-ready form. *See [Ch 16](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch16-ai-data-lifecycle.md).*

### Data detection and response

monitoring of data access patterns to alert on and respond to unusual or malicious activity. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

### Data diff

a row-by-row comparison of two versions of a table, used in CI or migrations to catch regressions before they ship. *See [Ch 13](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch13-data-quality-observability-lineage.md).*

### Data discovery

finding where data stores, and the sensitive data inside them, exist across an estate. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

### Data downtime

a period when data is late, missing, wrong or otherwise unreliable, by analogy with application downtime. *See [Ch 13](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch13-data-quality-observability-lineage.md).*

### Data drift

a change in the distribution of live model inputs relative to the training data. *See [Ch 21](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch21-ml-platforms-feature-stores-llmops.md).*

### Data flywheel

A loop in which product usage generates data (logs, traces, feedback) that improves the product and attracts more usage. *See [Ch 16](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch16-ai-data-lifecycle.md).*

### Data gravity

The tendency of large datasets to attract applications, compute and further data toward where they live. *See [Ch 01](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch01-data-stack-map.md).*

### Data inlining

DuckLake's technique of storing very small inserts, updates and deletes in the catalog database instead of writing new files. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Data leakage

information that would not be available at prediction time entering training data and inflating offline accuracy. *See [Ch 21](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch21-ml-platforms-feature-stores-llmops.md).*

### Data lineage

the directed graph of how data flows from sources through transformations to consumers such as dashboards, models and indexes. *See [Ch 13](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch13-data-quality-observability-lineage.md).*

### Data loss prevention

controls that detect and block sensitive data leaving approved boundaries. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

### Data metric function

a Snowflake function, scheduled on a table, that measures a quality metric such as row count, freshness or null count. *See [Ch 13](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch13-data-quality-observability-lineage.md).*

### Data mirroring

Continuous, vendor-managed replication of an operational database into an analytics platform (e.g., Fabric mirroring, Snowflake Postgres mirroring). *See [Ch 09](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch09-pipeline-patterns.md).*

### Data mixture

the proportions of each data source (web, code, math, books, synthetic) used at each stage of model training. *See [Ch 20](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch20-training-data-supply-chain.md).*

### Data observability

automated monitoring of dataset metadata (freshness, volume, schema, distribution, lineage) to detect, triage and explain data problems. *See [Ch 13](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch13-data-quality-observability-lineage.md).*

### Data poisoning

Inserting malicious examples into training or retrieval data to implant unwanted model behavior. *See [Ch 16](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch16-ai-data-lifecycle.md).*

### Data security posture management

continuous discovery of sensitive data, who can access it and where it is exposed, ranked by risk. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

### Data SLO

an internal service-level objective for a dataset's freshness, completeness or accuracy. *See [Ch 13](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch13-data-quality-observability-lineage.md).*

### Data sovereignty

legal requirements that certain data be stored and processed within a particular jurisdiction. *See [Ch 04](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch04-distributed-databases.md).*

### Data subject access request

an individual's legal request to see the personal data an organisation holds about them. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

### Data test

an explicit assertion, such as not-null, unique or accepted values, run against production data after a build. *See [Ch 13](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch13-data-quality-observability-lineage.md).*

### Data versioning

Recording immutable, addressable versions of datasets (e.g., lakeFS commits, table snapshots) so runs can be reproduced. *See [Ch 16](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch16-ai-data-lifecycle.md).*

### Database at hyperscaler

Oracle's model of running Exadata-based Oracle Database inside Azure, Google Cloud and AWS datacenters, sold through the host cloud (Oracle Database@Azure, @Google Cloud, @AWS). *See [Ch 28](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch28-hyperscaler-data-platforms.md).*

### Database branching

creating an instant, copy-on-write fork of a database for testing, previews or agent work. *See [Ch 22](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch22-agents-and-data.md).*

### dbt

Open-source framework that compiles SQL-plus-Jinja "models" into a dependency graph and runs them inside a warehouse or lakehouse. *See [Ch 12](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch12-transformation-and-orchestration.md).*

### DBU

Databricks Unit, the normalised unit of processing per hour that Databricks meters and prices by workload SKU. *See [Ch 25](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch25-databricks.md).*

### Declarative pipeline

A pipeline defined by the tables it should produce rather than the steps to run, e.g., Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines. *See [Ch 12](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch12-transformation-and-orchestration.md).*

### Declarative query

A query that states the result wanted and leaves the execution method to the database optimizer, as in SQL. *See [Ch 02](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch02-data-models.md).*

### Delete file

an Iceberg v2 file recording deleted rows either by file position or by column values. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Deletion vector

a compact bitmap marking which row positions in one data file are deleted, used by Delta Lake and Iceberg v3. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Delta checkpoint

a Parquet file summarising a Delta table's full state at one version so readers need not replay the whole log. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Delta encoding

compression that stores differences between consecutive values instead of the values themselves. *See [Ch 05](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch05-analytical-engines.md).*

### Delta Lake

Databricks' open table format: Parquet data files plus a JSON transaction log that gives ACID commits on object storage. *See [Ch 25](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch25-databricks.md).*

### Delta log

the `_delta_log` directory of numbered JSON commit files that records every change to a Delta Lake table. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Delta Sharing

Open REST protocol (2021) that shares tables by handing recipients short-lived signed URLs to the underlying files; now OpenSharing. *See [Ch 09](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch09-pipeline-patterns.md).*

### Denormalization

Deliberately duplicating data across records to make common reads cheaper at the cost of harder updates. *See [Ch 02](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch02-data-models.md).*

### Dictionary encoding

compression that replaces repeated values with small integer codes plus a lookup table. *See [Ch 05](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch05-analytical-engines.md).*

### Differential privacy

adding calibrated statistical noise to results so they reveal little about any single individual. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

### Digital twin

A live software model that mirrors physical or business entities and can push changes back to them. *See [Ch 31](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch31-analytical-engine-challengers-legacy.md).*

### Dimension

an attribute such as region or fiscal quarter used to group or filter measures. *See [Ch 14](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch14-semantic-layers-and-bi.md).*

### Direct preference optimization

A post-training method that learns directly from chosen/rejected answer pairs without a separate reward model (DPO). *See [Ch 16](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch16-ai-data-lifecycle.md).*

### Directed acyclic graph

A graph of tasks or models connected by one-way dependency edges with no cycles, used to determine run order. *See [Ch 12](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch12-transformation-and-orchestration.md).*

### Disaggregated shared-everything

VAST Data's storage architecture in which stateless servers access all flash enclosures over an NVMe fabric, so performance and capacity scale separately. *See [Ch 32](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch32-ai-native-data-companies.md).*

### Disaggregated storage

an architecture separating stateless compute from a shared storage service; in Aurora and Neon the storage consumes the database log. *See [Ch 04](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch04-distributed-databases.md).*

### DiskANN

Microsoft's SSD-resident graph vector index that keeps compressed vectors in DRAM and full vectors plus graph on flash. *See [Ch 18](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch18-embeddings-and-vector-search.md).*

### Diskless Kafka

Kafka-compatible designs whose primary store is object storage and whose brokers are stateless (e.g., WarpStream, KIP-1150). *See [Ch 11](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch11-streaming-and-event-platforms.md).*

### Distillation

training a smaller "student" model on the outputs of a larger "teacher" model. *See [Ch 20](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch20-training-data-supply-chain.md).*

### Document database

A database that stores self-contained JSON-like records (documents), such as MongoDB. *See [Ch 02](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch02-data-models.md).*

### Document parsing

converting a file into ordered text plus structure such as headings, tables and page references. *See [Ch 17](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch17-unstructured-data-processing.md).*

### DPU-hour

AWS Glue's billing unit: one data processing unit of compute running for one hour. *See [Ch 10](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch10-ingestion-and-integration.md).*

### DuckLake

a lakehouse format from the DuckDB team that stores all table metadata in a SQL database and data in Parquet. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Durable execution

A runtime model that persists each workflow step so code resumes exactly where it stopped after crashes or long waits. *See [Ch 12](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch12-transformation-and-orchestration.md).*

### Dynamic data masking

rewriting sensitive values at query time (for example, showing j***@example.com) without changing the stored data. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

### Dynamic table

A Snowflake table defined by a query and a target lag that the engine refreshes automatically, incrementally where possible. *See [Ch 12](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch12-transformation-and-orchestration.md).*

## E

### eCKU

Elastic Confluent Unit for Kafka, Confluent Cloud's capacity unit for metering cluster usage. *See [Ch 30](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch30-data-movement-streaming-companies.md).*

### EDP

AWS Enterprise Discount Program, AWS's historical name for its committed-spend discount contract. *See [Ch 28](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch28-hyperscaler-data-platforms.md).*

### Egress fee

a cloud provider's per-GB charge for data leaving its network or region. *See [Ch 24](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch24-data-meets-compute-and-storage.md).*

### ELT

Extract, load, transform: landing raw data first and transforming it inside the warehouse or lakehouse. *See [Ch 01](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch01-data-stack-map.md).*

### Embedding

A numeric vector produced by a model so that items with similar meaning lie close together. *See [Ch 02](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch02-data-models.md).*

### Enterprise Advanced

MongoDB's self-managed subscription offering with management tooling, security features and support. *See [Ch 29](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch29-operational-database-vendors.md).*

### Enterprise AI search

permission-aware search and AI assistants that index a company's own applications, documents and chat. *See [Ch 32](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch32-ai-native-data-companies.md).*

### Enterprise value

Market capitalisation plus debt minus cash, the value of the operating business to all capital providers. *See [Ch 27](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch27-databricks-vs-snowflake.md).*

### Entity resolution

linking records and detections across systems to the same real-world person or thing. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

### Equality delete

a delete expressed as column values (for example id = 5), cheap for streaming writers but expensive for readers. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Erasure coding

storing data as fragments plus parity so it survives failures with less capacity overhead than full replication. *See [Ch 24](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch24-data-meets-compute-and-storage.md).*

### ETL

Extract, transform, load: data is cleaned and reshaped on a separate system before it is loaded into the warehouse. *See [Ch 09](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch09-pipeline-patterns.md).*

### EV to NTM revenue

Enterprise value divided by expected revenue over the next twelve months, the standard software valuation multiple. *See [Ch 27](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch27-databricks-vs-snowflake.md).*

### Event streaming

Moving events continuously between systems through a durable, partitioned, append-only log such as Apache Kafka. *See [Ch 01](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch01-data-stack-map.md).*

### Event time

The time an event actually occurred, as opposed to the processing time at which the system observed it. *See [Ch 09](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch09-pipeline-patterns.md).*

### Eventual consistency

a consistency model promising only that replicas converge once writes stop. *See [Ch 04](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch04-distributed-databases.md).*

### Exact data match

detecting sensitive data by comparing content against hashed values from a known reference table. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

### Exactly-once semantics

A pipeline guarantee that each event affects the final result exactly once despite retries, achieved via deduplication or transactions. *See [Ch 09](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch09-pipeline-patterns.md).*

### Exadata

Oracle's engineered database hardware that pushes SQL filtering into storage servers connected by RDMA. *See [Ch 28](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch28-hyperscaler-data-platforms.md).*

### Execution accuracy

a text-to-SQL benchmark metric: the share of questions whose generated SQL returns the same result as the reference query. *See [Ch 22](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch22-agents-and-data.md).*

### Experiment tracking

logging each training run's parameters, metrics, code version and artifacts so runs can be compared and reproduced. *See [Ch 21](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch21-ml-platforms-feature-stores-llmops.md).*

### Expert data

training, demonstration and evaluation data written or judged by domain experts such as engineers, doctors or lawyers rather than crowd workers. *See [Ch 32](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch32-ai-native-data-companies.md).*

### Expert network

a data vendor that rents credentialed specialists (PhDs, doctors, engineers) by the hour to write or grade training data. *See [Ch 20](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch20-training-data-supply-chain.md).*

### EXPLAIN

the SQL command that shows the execution plan the optimizer chose, optionally with actual run-time statistics. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### Exposure

A declared downstream consumer of dbt models (dashboard, ML model, application) recorded in the project graph. *See [Ch 12](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch12-transformation-and-orchestration.md).*

### External consistency

the guarantee that transaction commit order matches real-time order across the whole system, as in Spanner. *See [Ch 04](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch04-distributed-databases.md).*

### External location

A Unity Catalog object that binds a storage path to a credential so governed tables and files can live there. *See [Ch 25](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch25-databricks.md).*

## F

### Fabless

A semiconductor company that designs chips but rents manufacturing capacity; used in the atlas as an analogy for Databricks and Snowflake. *See [Ch 28](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch28-hyperscaler-data-platforms.md).*

### Fair use

the US copyright defense that weighs a use's purpose, the work's nature, the amount used and the effect on the market. *See [Ch 20](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch20-training-data-supply-chain.md).*

### Faithfulness

A RAG metric for whether every claim in an answer is supported by the retrieved context. *See [Ch 19](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch19-retrieval-architectures.md).*

### Fan-out

the number of child pointers held by each internal page of a tree index, which sets the tree's height. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### Feature absorption

a standalone product's core function becoming a bundled feature of a larger platform, compressing the standalone vendor's pricing power. *See [Ch 32](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch32-ai-native-data-companies.md).*

### Feature store

a system that defines model features once and serves consistent values to both training and online inference. *See [Ch 21](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch21-ml-platforms-feature-stores-llmops.md).*

### First-party service

A partner's product that the cloud provider itself sells, bills and supports, such as Azure Databricks. *See [Ch 28](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch28-hyperscaler-data-platforms.md).*

### Five pillars of data observability

Monte Carlo's framing of the signals to monitor: freshness, volume, schema, distribution and lineage. *See [Ch 13](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch13-data-quality-observability-lineage.md).*

### Fixed-size chunking

splitting text every N tokens regardless of document structure. *See [Ch 17](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch17-unstructured-data-processing.md).*

### Flex Credits

Salesforce's consumption currency for Agentforce, priced per agent action. *See [Ch 34](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch34-application-giants-data-platforms.md).*

### Foreign key

A column whose values must match the primary key of another table, linking related rows. *See [Ch 02](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch02-data-models.md).*

### Format-preserving encryption

encryption whose output keeps the format of the input, such as a 16-digit number staying 16 digits. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

### Freight cluster

Confluent Cloud cluster type that writes directly to object storage, trading higher latency for much lower cost. *See [Ch 30](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch30-data-movement-streaming-companies.md).*

### Fsync

the operating-system call that forces buffered writes for a file onto stable storage. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

## G

### Genie

Databricks' natural-language analytics agent that turns questions into governed SQL, extended as Genie One in 2026. *See [Ch 25](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch25-databricks.md).*

### Global namespace

a single file-system view that spans many storage systems, sites and clouds. *See [Ch 32](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch32-ai-native-data-companies.md).*

### Golden set

a curated, versioned set of test inputs with reference answers used for regression-testing an AI application. *See [Ch 21](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch21-ml-platforms-feature-stores-llmops.md).*

### GPUDirect Storage

NVIDIA technology that moves data from storage directly into GPU memory by DMA, bypassing a copy through host DRAM. *See [Ch 24](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch24-data-meets-compute-and-storage.md).*

### GQL

Graph Query Language, the ISO/IEC 39075:2024 standard for querying property graphs, largely based on Cypher. *See [Ch 02](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch02-data-models.md).*

### Granule

ClickHouse's smallest unit of data read, 8,192 rows by default, addressed by one sparse-index entry. *See [Ch 23](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch23-real-time-analytics-htap.md).*

### Graph traversal

Answering a query by following edges from node to node, with cost proportional to edges touched. *See [Ch 02](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch02-data-models.md).*

### GraphRAG

Microsoft Research's 2024 approach that has an LLM extract an entity graph, cluster it into communities and pre-write summaries for answering corpus-wide questions. *See [Ch 19](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch19-retrieval-architectures.md).*

### Group commit

making several concurrently committing transactions durable with a single log flush. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### Growth-adjusted multiple

A valuation multiple divided by the revenue growth rate, used to compare companies growing at different speeds. *See [Ch 27](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch27-databricks-vs-snowflake.md).*

### Guardrails

input and output checks that block prompt injection, data leakage or unsafe and off-policy LLM responses. *See [Ch 21](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch21-ml-platforms-feature-stores-llmops.md).*

## H

### Headless BI

a semantic layer decoupled from any single visualization tool and served to many consumers via APIs. *See [Ch 14](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch14-semantic-layers-and-bi.md).*

### Hidden partitioning

Iceberg's practice of deriving partition values from column transforms so queries filter on ordinary columns and never reference partitions. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Hive Metastore

Apache Hive's Thrift service backed by a relational database that records tables, columns and partitions; the first widely shared lakehouse catalog. *See [Ch 08](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch08-catalogs-and-metastores.md).*

### HNSW

Hierarchical Navigable Small World, a layered proximity-graph vector index searched by greedy descent from sparse to dense layers. *See [Ch 18](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch18-embeddings-and-vector-search.md).*

### Horizon Catalog

Snowflake's built-in governance, discovery and access-control layer for data and AI objects. *See [Ch 27](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch27-databricks-vs-snowflake.md).*

### Hot spot

a shard or key that receives disproportionate traffic and limits the throughput of the whole cluster. *See [Ch 04](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch04-distributed-databases.md).*

### HTAP

Hybrid transactional/analytical processing: one system serving OLTP and OLAP workloads on fresh data (term coined by Gartner, 2014). *See [Ch 01](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch01-data-stack-map.md).*

### Hudi timeline

Apache Hudi's ordered record of table actions (commits, compactions, cleans), each moving from requested to inflight to completed. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Hybrid data platform

A single data software stack designed to run both on-premises and in public clouds with the same tools and governance. *See [Ch 31](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch31-analytical-engine-challengers-legacy.md).*

### Hybrid logical clock

a timestamp combining physical clock time with a logical counter, used by CockroachDB and YugabyteDB to order events without special hardware. *See [Ch 04](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch04-distributed-databases.md).*

### Hybrid search

Combining keyword (BM25) and vector retrieval, usually followed by a reranker. *See [Ch 18](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch18-embeddings-and-vector-search.md).*

### HyDE

Hypothetical Document Embeddings: retrieving with the embedding of an LLM-written hypothetical answer instead of the raw question. *See [Ch 19](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch19-retrieval-architectures.md).*

### Hyperscaler

A cloud provider operating at global datacenter scale, chiefly AWS, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud, often with Oracle OCI included. *See [Ch 28](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch28-hyperscaler-data-platforms.md).*

## I

### Iceberg REST catalog

the open HTTP API specification through which engines load, commit to and increasingly plan scans on Iceberg tables. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Icehouse

Starburst's name for a lakehouse built on the Trino engine and Apache Iceberg tables on object storage. *See [Ch 31](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch31-analytical-engine-challengers-legacy.md).*

### Idempotency

The property that running an operation more than once produces the same result as running it once. *See [Ch 09](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch09-pipeline-patterns.md).*

### Idempotent producer

A Kafka producer that stamps batches with sequence numbers so broker-side deduplication makes retries harmless. *See [Ch 11](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch11-streaming-and-event-platforms.md).*

### Identity propagation

passing the end user's identity through every hop so downstream systems enforce that user's permissions rather than a service account's. *See [Ch 22](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch22-agents-and-data.md).*

### Illiquidity discount

The reduction in value applied to shares that cannot be freely sold on a public market. *See [Ch 27](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch27-databricks-vs-snowflake.md).*

### Impact analysis

using downstream lineage to find every asset and owner affected by a proposed or actual change. *See [Ch 13](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch13-data-quality-observability-lineage.md).*

### In-process database

A database engine that runs as a library inside the application's process, with no separate server (e.g., SQLite, DuckDB). *See [Ch 23](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch23-real-time-analytics-htap.md).*

### In-sync replicas

The replicas fully caught up with a partition's leader (ISR); all must hold a write before an acks=all acknowledgment. *See [Ch 11](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch11-streaming-and-event-platforms.md).*

### Incremental model

A transformation that processes only new or changed rows and merges them into an existing table instead of rebuilding it. *See [Ch 12](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch12-transformation-and-orchestration.md).*

### Incremental snapshot

A chunked, lock-free copy of a table that is interleaved with a live CDC stream using watermark markers (DBLog/Debezium). *See [Ch 09](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch09-pipeline-patterns.md).*

### Incremental sync

fetching only the records that changed since the last successful sync. *See [Ch 10](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch10-ingestion-and-integration.md).*

### Informatica Processing Unit

Informatica's pre-paid, pooled consumption unit that can be spent across IDMC services. *See [Ch 10](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch10-ingestion-and-integration.md).*

### Integrated device manufacturer

A semiconductor company that both designs and fabricates its chips; used in the atlas as an analogy for hyperscalers. *See [Ch 28](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch28-hyperscaler-data-platforms.md).*

### Inter-AZ data transfer

The per-GB cloud charge for network traffic between availability zones in the same region. *See [Ch 11](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch11-streaming-and-event-platforms.md).*

### Inverted index

A search index mapping each term to the list of documents that contain it. *See [Ch 02](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch02-data-models.md).*

### iPaaS

integration platform as a service, used mainly to connect operational applications through APIs and events. *See [Ch 10](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch10-ingestion-and-integration.md).*

### Isolation level

a setting that defines which concurrency anomalies a database allows transactions to observe. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### IVF

Inverted file index: clusters vectors with k-means and searches only the clusters nearest the query (set by nprobe). *See [Ch 18](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch18-embeddings-and-vector-search.md).*

### IVF-PQ

A vector index combining IVF clustering with product-quantized vectors, standard for billion-scale search on one machine or GPU. *See [Ch 18](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch18-embeddings-and-vector-search.md).*

## J

### Jaccard similarity

the size of two sets' intersection divided by the size of their union, used to measure near-duplicate text. *See [Ch 20](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch20-training-data-supply-chain.md).*

### Jinja

The Python templating language dbt uses for macros, control flow and functions such as ref(). *See [Ch 12](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch12-transformation-and-orchestration.md).*

### Join

A query operation that combines rows from two or more tables on matching key values. *See [Ch 02](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch02-data-models.md).*

## K

### k-nearest neighbors

Exact search for the k stored vectors closest to a query, comparing against every vector. *See [Ch 18](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch18-embeddings-and-vector-search.md).*

### Key-value store

A database that stores and retrieves an opaque value by its unique key, like a distributed hash table. *See [Ch 02](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch02-data-models.md).*

### Knowledge Catalog

Google Cloud's governance and metadata catalog, renamed in 2026 from Dataplex Universal Catalog. *See [Ch 28](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch28-hyperscaler-data-platforms.md).*

### Knowledge graph

A store of entities and typed relationships between them, queried by traversal. *See [Ch 19](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch19-retrieval-architectures.md).*

### KRaft

Kafka's built-in Raft-based metadata quorum, which replaced ZooKeeper and became mandatory in Kafka 4.0. *See [Ch 11](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch11-streaming-and-event-platforms.md).*

### KV cache

The attention keys and values a transformer stores for tokens already processed, so they need not be recomputed; it grows linearly with context length. *See [Ch 19](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch19-retrieval-architectures.md).*

## L

### Lakebase

Databricks' serverless Postgres database, built on the Neon acquisition, with compute separated from object-storage-backed storage. *See [Ch 25](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch25-databricks.md).*

### Lakeflow

Databricks' suite for data ingestion, declarative pipelines and job orchestration. *See [Ch 25](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch25-databricks.md).*

### Lakehouse

an architecture that provides warehouse-grade management and performance over open file and table formats on object storage. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Lance

LanceDB's open columnar file format and table layer, designed for fast random access, versioning and multimodal/vector AI data. *See [Ch 06](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch06-file-formats.md).*

### Late chunking

embedding a whole document with a long-context model first, then pooling token vectors into chunk vectors. *See [Ch 17](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch17-unstructured-data-processing.md).*

### Late data

Events that arrive after the watermark has passed the end of their window, and are either dropped or used to correct results. *See [Ch 09](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch09-pipeline-patterns.md).*

### Late materialization

deferring assembly of full rows until filters have reduced the data to the matching positions. *See [Ch 05](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch05-analytical-engines.md).*

### Layout analysis

detecting a page's regions (headings, paragraphs, tables, figures) and how they relate. *See [Ch 17](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch17-unstructured-data-processing.md).*

### Leaderless replication

a Dynamo-style topology in which clients write to and read from quorums of replicas directly, with no single leader. *See [Ch 04](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch04-distributed-databases.md).*

### Lethal trifecta

the risky combination, in one agent, of access to private data, exposure to untrusted content and a channel to send data out. *See [Ch 22](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch22-agents-and-data.md).*

### Linearizability

a consistency model in which every operation appears to take effect at one instant consistent with real time. *See [Ch 04](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch04-distributed-databases.md).*

### Liquidation preference

The right of preferred shareholders to be repaid before common shareholders in a sale or liquidation. *See [Ch 25](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch25-databricks.md).*

### LLM evaluation

systematic scoring of LLM application outputs, offline on curated test sets or online on sampled production traffic. *See [Ch 21](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch21-ml-platforms-feature-stores-llmops.md).*

### LLM judge

A language model used to grade other models' outputs against a rubric. *See [Ch 16](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch16-ai-data-lifecycle.md).*

### LLM trace

a record of every step, token count, latency and cost in a single LLM or agent request. *See [Ch 21](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch21-ml-platforms-feature-stores-llmops.md).*

### LLM-as-judge

Using a language model to grade another model's outputs against a rubric or reference. *See [Ch 19](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch19-retrieval-architectures.md).*

### LLMOps

MLOps adapted to LLM applications, managing prompts, traces, evaluations, guardrails and gateways instead of mainly model weights. *See [Ch 21](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch21-ml-platforms-feature-stores-llmops.md).*

### Locality-sensitive hashing

hashing that puts similar items into the same bucket so only likely matches are compared (LSH). *See [Ch 20](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch20-training-data-supply-chain.md).*

### Log compaction

A Kafka retention mode that keeps only the latest record for each key, turning a topic into a changelog of current state. *See [Ch 11](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch11-streaming-and-event-platforms.md).*

### Log-based CDC

Change data capture that reads the database's recovery log (Postgres WAL, MySQL binlog, Oracle redo) instead of querying tables. *See [Ch 09](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch09-pipeline-patterns.md).*

### LookML

Looker's code-based, Git-versioned language for defining semantic models that generate SQL. *See [Ch 14](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch14-semantic-layers-and-bi.md).*

### Lost in the middle

The finding (Liu et al., 2023) that language models use information at the start and end of long inputs better than information in the middle. *See [Ch 19](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch19-retrieval-architectures.md).*

### LSM-tree

a log-structured merge tree, a write-optimised structure that buffers writes and merges sorted runs in the background. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Luhn checksum

a check-digit algorithm used to validate candidate payment-card numbers and reject most random digit strings. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

## M

### MACC

Microsoft Azure Consumption Commitment, Microsoft's committed-spend contract, which eligible Azure Marketplace purchases can draw down. *See [Ch 28](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch28-hyperscaler-data-platforms.md).*

### Managed storage

vendor-operated tiered storage (local SSD cache plus object storage) behind a warehouse, as in Redshift RA3. *See [Ch 05](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch05-analytical-engines.md).*

### Manifest

an Iceberg Avro file listing data or delete files with their partition values and per-column statistics. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Manifest list

an Iceberg file listing the manifests that make up one snapshot, with partition-range summaries used to skip manifests. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Marketplace drawdown

Counting purchases made through a cloud marketplace against the customer's committed spend with that cloud. *See [Ch 28](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch28-hyperscaler-data-platforms.md).*

### Marquez

the open-source LF AI & Data reference implementation that collects, stores and serves OpenLineage events. *See [Ch 13](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch13-data-quality-observability-lineage.md).*

### Massively parallel processing

spreading a query across many nodes that each process a slice of the data in parallel (MPP). *See [Ch 05](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch05-analytical-engines.md).*

### Master data management

Software and process that resolves duplicate records about the same customer, product or supplier into one trusted "golden record". *See [Ch 30](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch30-data-movement-streaming-companies.md).*

### Materialization

How a dbt model's result is persisted: as a view, table, incremental table or ephemeral CTE. *See [Ch 12](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch12-transformation-and-orchestration.md).*

### Materialized view

A stored query result kept up to date as source data changes; in ClickHouse, an insert trigger that writes pre-aggregated rows. *See [Ch 23](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch23-real-time-analytics-htap.md).*

### Matryoshka embedding

An embedding trained so its leading dimensions form a usable shorter embedding, allowing truncation. *See [Ch 18](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch18-embeddings-and-vector-search.md).*

### MCP server

a service that wraps one system and exposes tools, resources and prompts to AI agents over the Model Context Protocol. *See [Ch 22](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch22-agents-and-data.md).*

### MDX

Multidimensional Expressions, Microsoft-originated query language for OLAP cubes. *See [Ch 14](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch14-semantic-layers-and-bi.md).*

### Measure

an aggregation with business rules (e.g., net revenue = gross minus refunds) defined in a semantic model. *See [Ch 14](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch14-semantic-layers-and-bi.md).*

### Medallion architecture

Layering data into bronze (raw), silver (cleaned and conformed) and gold (business-ready) tables. *See [Ch 09](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch09-pipeline-patterns.md).*

### Memtable

the in-memory, sorted write buffer of an LSM-tree that is flushed to disk when full. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### Merge-on-read

applying row-level changes by writing separate delete or change records that readers merge at query time until compaction. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### MergeTree

ClickHouse's core table engine: sorted, immutable columnar parts written per insert and merged in the background. *See [Ch 23](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch23-real-time-analytics-htap.md).*

### Metadata pointer

the catalog's record of which metadata file represents a table's current version; swapping it atomically is an Iceberg commit. *See [Ch 08](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch08-catalogs-and-metastores.md).*

### Metastore

a service that stores table definitions, schemas and locations so query engines can find data; the Hive-era name for a technical catalog. *See [Ch 08](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch08-catalogs-and-metastores.md).*

### Metric view

a Databricks Unity Catalog object that defines governed, reusable business metrics queryable via SQL. *See [Ch 14](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch14-semantic-layers-and-bi.md).*

### MetricFlow

dbt's metric-definition and SQL-generation engine behind the dbt Semantic Layer, open-sourced under Apache 2.0 in Oct 2025. *See [Ch 14](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch14-semantic-layers-and-bi.md).*

### Metrics layer

a semantic layer focused on defining metrics once for reuse across tools; often used interchangeably with semantic layer. *See [Ch 14](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch14-semantic-layers-and-bi.md).*

### Micro-batch

Processing a stream as a rapid series of small batch jobs, typically every few seconds to minutes. *See [Ch 09](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch09-pipeline-patterns.md).*

### Micro-partition

Snowflake's immutable columnar storage unit (50–500 MB uncompressed) carrying per-column metadata for pruning. *See [Ch 05](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch05-analytical-engines.md).*

### Microsoft Fabric

Microsoft's SaaS analytics suite (pipelines, Spark, warehouse, real-time, Power BI) built on OneLake and capacity pricing. *See [Ch 28](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch28-hyperscaler-data-platforms.md).*

### MinHash

A hashing technique that cheaply estimates set similarity between documents, used for near-duplicate removal at web scale. *See [Ch 16](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch16-ai-data-lifecycle.md).*

### MLOps

practices and tools that make the machine-learning lifecycle (data, features, training, registry, serving, monitoring) repeatable, governed and monitored. *See [Ch 21](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch21-ml-platforms-feature-stores-llmops.md).*

### Model checkpoint

A saved snapshot of model weights and optimizer state used to resume, roll back or audit training. *See [Ch 16](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch16-ai-data-lifecycle.md).*

### Model collapse

progressive degradation when models train recursively on model-generated data and lose the rare tails of the real distribution. *See [Ch 20](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch20-training-data-supply-chain.md).*

### Model Context Protocol

An open standard (MCP), introduced by Anthropic in 2024, for exposing tools and data sources to AI agents. *See [Ch 01](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch01-data-stack-map.md).*

### Model contract

A dbt feature that fails a model's build if its output columns or data types drift from a declared shape. *See [Ch 12](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch12-transformation-and-orchestration.md).*

### Model registry

a catalog of model versions with lineage, lifecycle stages and approvals used to promote models to production. *See [Ch 21](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch21-ml-platforms-feature-stores-llmops.md).*

### Monthly active rows

Fivetran's billing unit: distinct rows inserted, updated or deleted in a month, tiered per connection since March 2025. *See [Ch 09](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch09-pipeline-patterns.md).*

### MTEB

Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, the standard public leaderboard for embedding models (extended as MMTEB). *See [Ch 18](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch18-embeddings-and-vector-search.md).*

### Multi-leader replication

a topology in which several replicas accept writes and exchange them, so conflicting writes must be resolved. *See [Ch 04](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch04-distributed-databases.md).*

### Multi-model database

A single database engine that supports several data models, such as tables, JSON documents and vectors. *See [Ch 02](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch02-data-models.md).*

### MVCC

multi-version concurrency control: keeping several versions of a row so readers and writers do not block each other. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

## N

### Named-entity recognition

machine learning that tags names, places, organisations and similar entities in free text. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

### Namespace

a hierarchical container, such as a database or schema, that groups tables inside a catalog. *See [Ch 08](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch08-catalogs-and-metastores.md).*

### NDJSON

Newline-delimited JSON: a text file with one self-contained JSON record per line, easy to stream but costly to parse. *See [Ch 06](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch06-file-formats.md).*

### Needle in a haystack

A long-context test that hides one fact in filler text and asks the model to retrieve it; it measures lookup rather than reasoning. *See [Ch 19](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch19-retrieval-architectures.md).*

### Net revenue retention

This year's spend from last year's customer cohort divided by that cohort's spend a year earlier. *See [Ch 25](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch25-databricks.md).*

### NewSQL

distributed databases that offer SQL and ACID transactions at horizontal scale, also called distributed SQL. *See [Ch 04](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch04-distributed-databases.md).*

### Nimble

Meta's open-source columnar file format aimed at very wide machine-learning feature tables. *See [Ch 06](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch06-file-formats.md).*

### Normalization

Structuring relational tables so each fact is stored exactly once, avoiding update anomalies. *See [Ch 02](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch02-data-models.md).*

## O

### Object storage

flat, HTTP-accessed storage of immutable objects addressed by key, such as Amazon S3. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### ODCS

Open Data Contract Standard, a YAML specification for data contracts maintained by the Linux Foundation's Bitol project. *See [Ch 12](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch12-transformation-and-orchestration.md).*

### OEM

Original equipment manufacturer arrangement: one vendor embeds and resells another vendor's product inside its own offering. *See [Ch 31](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch31-analytical-engine-challengers-legacy.md).*

### Offline store

the part of a feature store that keeps full timestamped feature history, usually lakehouse tables, for building training sets. *See [Ch 21](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch21-ml-platforms-feature-stores-llmops.md).*

### Offset

The sequential position number of a record within a partition. *See [Ch 11](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch11-streaming-and-event-platforms.md).*

### OLAP

Online analytical processing: large scans and aggregations across historical data, usually on columnar storage. *See [Ch 01](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch01-data-stack-map.md).*

### OLAP cube

a pre-aggregated multidimensional data structure for fast slice-and-dice analysis, typically queried with MDX. *See [Ch 14](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch14-semantic-layers-and-bi.md).*

### OLTP

Online transaction processing: many small, fast, correct reads and writes that record business events such as orders and payments. *See [Ch 01](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch01-data-stack-map.md).*

### On-behalf-of flow

an OAuth token exchange in which a service or agent obtains a token to act for a specific user. *See [Ch 22](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch22-agents-and-data.md).*

### OneLake

Microsoft Fabric's single tenant-wide logical data lake that stores tables as Delta/Parquet. *See [Ch 28](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch28-hyperscaler-data-platforms.md).*

### OneLake shortcut

A pointer that mounts data from ADLS, S3, Google Cloud Storage or other stores into OneLake without copying it. *See [Ch 28](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch28-hyperscaler-data-platforms.md).*

### Online store

the part of a feature store that keeps the latest feature values per entity in a low-latency key-value database for inference. *See [Ch 21](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch21-ml-platforms-feature-stores-llmops.md).*

### Ontology

A governed model of an organisation's business objects, their properties, links and permitted actions, such as Palantir's Foundry Ontology. *See [Ch 19](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch19-retrieval-architectures.md).*

### Open core

A business model that gives away an open-source core product and sells proprietary features, support or a hosted service around it. *See [Ch 30](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch30-data-movement-streaming-companies.md).*

### Open Policy Agent

a CNCF graduated, general-purpose policy engine that evaluates rules written in the Rego language. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

### Open Semantic Interchange

Snowflake-convened cross-vendor initiative (2025) and Apache-licensed spec for portable semantic models. *See [Ch 14](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch14-semantic-layers-and-bi.md).*

### Open table format

an openly governed metadata layer and commit protocol that turns a collection of files on object storage into a transactional table with snapshots and schema evolution. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### OpenLineage

an open LF AI & Data specification for lineage events (run, job, input and output datasets, facets) emitted by data jobs at runtime. *See [Ch 13](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch13-data-quality-observability-lineage.md).*

### OpenSharing

Linux Foundation open protocol for sharing data and AI assets across platforms, the successor to Delta Sharing (2026). *See [Ch 09](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch09-pipeline-patterns.md).*

### Optical character recognition

converting images of text into machine-readable characters, usually with a confidence score for each word (OCR). *See [Ch 17](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch17-unstructured-data-processing.md).*

### Optimistic concurrency control

a scheme where writers work without locks and validate at commit time, retrying if another writer committed first. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Orchestrator

Software that schedules, triggers, runs, retries and records data or application workflows. *See [Ch 12](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch12-transformation-and-orchestration.md).*

### Orphan file

a file in a table's storage location that no snapshot references, typically left by a failed or abandoned write. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

## P

### PACELC

Abadi's extension of CAP: under a partition choose availability or consistency, else choose latency or consistency. *See [Ch 04](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch04-distributed-databases.md).*

### Page

the fixed-size block (for example 8 kB in PostgreSQL, 16 KB in InnoDB) that is a database's unit of I/O and caching. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### Page split

dividing a full B-tree page into two pages and inserting a new separator key into the parent. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### PagedAttention

vLLM's technique of storing the attention key-value cache in fixed-size pages, like virtual memory, to raise GPU utilisation. *See [Ch 21](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch21-ml-platforms-feature-stores-llmops.md).*

### Parallel NFS

an extension of the NFS protocol (pNFS, NFS v4.1+) that lets clients read and write data on many storage servers in parallel. *See [Ch 32](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch32-ai-native-data-companies.md).*

### Parquet

the dominant open columnar file format for analytics, used beneath all major table formats. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Partition

An independently ordered shard of a Kafka topic and the unit of parallelism and ordering. *See [Ch 11](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch11-streaming-and-event-platforms.md).*

### Partition evolution

changing a table's partitioning scheme for new data without rewriting existing files. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Partition key

The attribute whose hashed value decides which partition or node stores a record. *See [Ch 02](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch02-data-models.md).*

### Paxos

Leslie Lamport's consensus protocol, used in production as Multi-Paxos by Spanner and many Google systems. *See [Ch 04](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch04-distributed-databases.md).*

### Permission-aware retrieval

filtering retrieval candidates by the caller's identity and the stored ACLs before ranking. *See [Ch 17](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch17-unstructured-data-processing.md).*

### Personally identifiable information

data that can identify an individual, such as names, IDs or contact details (PII). *See [Ch 17](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch17-unstructured-data-processing.md).*

### pgvector

The open-source PostgreSQL extension for storing embeddings and running exact or approximate nearest-neighbour search. *See [Ch 29](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch29-operational-database-vendors.md).*

### Photon

Databricks' vectorized C++ query engine that replaces Spark's JVM execution for supported operators. *See [Ch 25](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch25-databricks.md).*

### PII

Personally identifiable information, such as names, emails and ID numbers, that must be removed or access-controlled. *See [Ch 16](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch16-ai-data-lifecycle.md).*

### Point-in-time join

a join that attaches to each training label the most recent feature values known at the label's timestamp, preventing leakage. *See [Ch 21](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch21-ml-platforms-feature-stores-llmops.md).*

### Policy engine

software that evaluates access rules and returns allow, deny, filter or mask decisions for enforcement points. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

### Post-filtering

Applying metadata filters after vector search, simple but able to return too few results. *See [Ch 18](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch18-embeddings-and-vector-search.md).*

### Post-money valuation

The latest private round's price per share multiplied by all fully diluted shares after the round. *See [Ch 27](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch27-databricks-vs-snowflake.md).*

### Post-training

The stages after pretraining (supervised fine-tuning, preference tuning, reinforcement learning) that turn a base model into an assistant. *See [Ch 16](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch16-ai-data-lifecycle.md).*

### Postgres extension

An add-on module that adds data types, index methods or functions to PostgreSQL without forking the core engine. *See [Ch 29](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch29-operational-database-vendors.md).*

### Pre-filtering

Applying metadata filters before vector search, exact but able to fragment graph indexes. *See [Ch 18](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch18-embeddings-and-vector-search.md).*

### Precedent transaction

A past acquisition whose price multiples (e.g., EV/revenue) are used as a benchmark for valuing a comparable company. *See [Ch 30](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch30-data-movement-streaming-companies.md).*

### Predicate pushdown

Using file or row-group statistics (min/max, null counts) to skip data that a query's filter cannot match. *See [Ch 06](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch06-file-formats.md).*

### Preference data

Pairs or rankings of model outputs labeled by which is better, used for RLHF or DPO. *See [Ch 16](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch16-ai-data-lifecycle.md).*

### Pretraining

Training a model to predict the next token over a very large, general corpus such as filtered web text. *See [Ch 16](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch16-ai-data-lifecycle.md).*

### Primary key

The column or set of columns that uniquely identifies each row in a table. *See [Ch 02](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch02-data-models.md).*

### Product quantization

Vector compression that splits each vector into slices and stores each slice as an index into a learned codebook. *See [Ch 18](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch18-embeddings-and-vector-search.md).*

### Project Aether

NVIDIA tooling, announced at GTC 2025, that qualifies, tests and tunes Spark jobs for GPU acceleration. *See [Ch 24](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch24-data-meets-compute-and-storage.md).*

### Prompt caching

Reusing an already-processed prompt prefix across requests at a discounted token price and lower latency. *See [Ch 19](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch19-retrieval-architectures.md).*

### Prompt injection

malicious instructions embedded in content an LLM reads, causing it to act against its user. *See [Ch 22](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch22-agents-and-data.md).*

### Property graph

A graph data model of nodes and edges where both can carry key-value properties. *See [Ch 02](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch02-data-models.md).*

### Pseudonymisation

processing personal data so it cannot be attributed to a person without separately held information; still personal data under GDPR. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

### Puffin file

Iceberg's file format for auxiliary blobs such as statistics sketches and v3 deletion vectors. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*
