### Purpose limitation

the principle that personal data be collected and used only for specified, compatible purposes. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

## Q

### Quality classifier

A small model that scores documents for training value so only high-scoring text is kept. *See [Ch 16](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch16-ai-data-lifecycle.md).*

### Query compilation

generating machine code for each query so operators fuse into tight loops (e.g., HyPer, Spark whole-stage codegen). *See [Ch 05](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch05-analytical-engines.md).*

### Query federation

Querying external databases in place by pushing queries down to them rather than copying their data. *See [Ch 09](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch09-pipeline-patterns.md).*

### Query optimizer

the database component that chooses an execution plan for a query, usually by estimating costs. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### Query-based CDC

Change data capture that polls tables for rows with a newer timestamp or ID; simple but misses hard deletes. *See [Ch 09](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch09-pipeline-patterns.md).*

### Query-log mining

parsing a warehouse's history of executed SQL to infer lineage, usage and table importance. *See [Ch 13](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch13-data-quality-observability-lineage.md).*

### Quorum

the minimum number of replicas, usually a majority, that must acknowledge an operation for it to count. *See [Ch 04](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch04-distributed-databases.md).*

## R

### Raft

a consensus protocol designed for understandability, built from leader election, log replication and majority commit. *See [Ch 04](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch04-distributed-databases.md).*

### RAPIDS

NVIDIA's open-source suite of CUDA libraries (cuDF, cuML, cuVS and others) for GPU data science and data processing. *See [Ch 24](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch24-data-meets-compute-and-storage.md).*

### RAPIDS Accelerator for Apache Spark

an NVIDIA plugin that replaces Spark SQL and DataFrame operators with GPU versions without user code changes. *See [Ch 24](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch24-data-meets-compute-and-storage.md).*

### Rate limit

a cap on API calls per time window imposed by a source system. *See [Ch 10](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch10-ingestion-and-integration.md).*

### RDF

Resource Description Framework, a graph model of subject–predicate–object triples queried with SPARQL. *See [Ch 02](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch02-data-models.md).*

### Read amplification

the number of storage reads a database performs per logical lookup. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### Read-after-write consistency

a guarantee that a successful write is immediately visible to every later read and listing; S3 has provided it since December 2020. *See [Ch 24](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch24-data-meets-compute-and-storage.md).*

### Reading order

the sequence in which a human would read a page's text blocks, which parsers must reconstruct from glyph positions. *See [Ch 17](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch17-unstructured-data-processing.md).*

### Real-time analytics

Sub-second analytical queries over data that is seconds old, served at high concurrency to apps, users or agents. *See [Ch 23](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch23-real-time-analytics-htap.md).*

### Recall at k

The share of the true k nearest neighbours that an approximate index actually returns. *See [Ch 18](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch18-embeddings-and-vector-search.md).*

### Reciprocal rank fusion

A method for merging ranked lists that scores each item by the sum of 1/(k + rank) across lists, with k = 60 by convention (RRF). *See [Ch 19](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch19-retrieval-architectures.md).*

### Recursive chunking

splitting by progressively finer separators (paragraph, sentence, word) until chunks fit a size limit. *See [Ch 17](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch17-unstructured-data-processing.md).*

### Red-teaming

Adversarial human or automated testing to find unsafe or unintended model behavior. *See [Ch 16](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch16-ai-data-lifecycle.md).*

### Reinforcement learning from AI feedback

RLHF in which a model, guided by written principles, produces the preference labels (RLAIF). *See [Ch 16](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch16-ai-data-lifecycle.md).*

### Reinforcement learning from human feedback

Tuning a model with reinforcement learning against a reward learned from human preference rankings (RLHF). *See [Ch 16](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch16-ai-data-lifecycle.md).*

### Relational model

A way of storing data as tables of rows linked by key values and queried declaratively, proposed by E. F. Codd in 1970. *See [Ch 02](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch02-data-models.md).*

### Remaining performance obligations

Contracted revenue a company has not yet recognised, i.e. its reported backlog. *See [Ch 28](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch28-hyperscaler-data-platforms.md).*

### Remote signing

a catalog signing each object-storage request on an engine's behalf instead of handing out credentials. *See [Ch 08](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch08-catalogs-and-metastores.md).*

### Replication

keeping copies of the same data on several nodes for durability and availability. *See [Ch 04](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch04-distributed-databases.md).*

### Replication lag

the delay between a write committing on the leader and becoming visible on a replica. *See [Ch 04](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch04-distributed-databases.md).*

### Replication slot

A Postgres object that makes the primary retain write-ahead log until a consumer confirms it has read it. *See [Ch 09](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch09-pipeline-patterns.md).*

### Request pricing

per-call charges for object-storage operations such as PUT, GET and LIST, which make many small files expensive. *See [Ch 24](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch24-data-meets-compute-and-storage.md).*

### Reranker

A second-stage model, usually a cross-encoder, that reorders a short list of retrieved candidates by relevance. *See [Ch 19](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch19-retrieval-architectures.md).*

### Rescoring

Re-ranking candidates found with compressed vectors using their full-precision vectors. *See [Ch 18](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch18-embeddings-and-vector-search.md).*

### Retrieval-augmented generation

Fetching relevant content at query time and adding it to a language model's prompt (RAG). *See [Ch 01](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch01-data-stack-map.md).*

### Revenue run-rate

Current-period revenue annualised (e.g., quarterly revenue times four); not audited annual revenue. *See [Ch 25](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch25-databricks.md).*

### Reverse ETL

Syncing modeled data from the warehouse back into operational SaaS tools such as CRM and ad platforms. *See [Ch 09](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch09-pipeline-patterns.md).*

### Reward model

A model trained on human rankings of outputs that scores new outputs during reinforcement learning. *See [Ch 16](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch16-ai-data-lifecycle.md).*

### Right to erasure

the GDPR right to have personal data deleted in defined circumstances (Article 17). *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

### RL environment

A sandboxed replica of a task, website or software system in which an AI agent acts and is automatically scored. *See [Ch 16](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch16-ai-data-lifecycle.md).*

### Role explosion

the proliferation of narrowly scoped roles that occurs when RBAC is used to express many combinations of sensitivity, region and purpose. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

### Role-based access control

a model in which permissions are granted to roles and users receive access by being assigned roles. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

### Row group

A horizontal slice of rows in a Parquet file; the unit that predicate pushdown can skip as a whole. *See [Ch 06](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch06-file-formats.md).*

### Row lineage

Iceberg v3 tracking of a stable row ID and last-updated sequence number for each row. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Row store

a layout that keeps all of a row's columns together on a page, suited to transactional reads and writes. *See [Ch 05](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch05-analytical-engines.md).*

### Row-level security

a policy that silently filters which rows of a table a given user can see. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

### RUM conjecture

the 2016 claim that an access method cannot minimize read, update and memory overhead all at once. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### Run-length encoding

compression that stores a value once with a count of how many times it repeats consecutively. *See [Ch 05](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch05-analytical-engines.md).*

## S

### S3 Express One Zone

AWS's single-Availability-Zone, low-latency S3 storage class that uses directory buckets, often used as a hot tier for tables and training data. *See [Ch 24](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch24-data-meets-compute-and-storage.md).*

### S3 Tables

AWS's managed Apache Iceberg tables stored in S3 "table buckets", with automatic compaction and snapshot clean-up. *See [Ch 28](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch28-hyperscaler-data-platforms.md).*

### S3 Vectors

AWS's vector storage and similarity-search capability built into S3, GA at re:Invent 2025. *See [Ch 28](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch28-hyperscaler-data-platforms.md).*

### Safetensors

A tensor file format (JSON header plus raw buffers) that can be memory-mapped and cannot execute code on load, unlike pickle checkpoints. *See [Ch 06](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch06-file-formats.md).*

### Scalar quantization

Storing each vector coordinate in fewer bits, such as int8 instead of float32, for a 4x size cut. *See [Ch 18](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch18-embeddings-and-vector-search.md).*

### Scale-to-zero

releasing all compute for an idle database or service so it costs only storage until the next request. *See [Ch 22](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch22-agents-and-data.md).*

### ScaNN

Google's vector search method using anisotropic quantization, used in AlloyDB and Vertex AI Vector Search. *See [Ch 18](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch18-embeddings-and-vector-search.md).*

### Schema drift

unplanned changes in a source's columns or data types that a pipeline must detect and handle. *See [Ch 10](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch10-ingestion-and-integration.md).*

### Schema evolution

safely adding, dropping, renaming, reordering or widening columns over a table's life without rewriting data. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Schema linking

selecting the relevant tables, columns and joins from a large schema before an LLM generates SQL. *See [Ch 22](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch22-agents-and-data.md).*

### Schema Registry

A service (e.g., Confluent's) that stores versioned schemas for streaming topics and rejects changes that would break consumers. *See [Ch 06](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch06-file-formats.md).*

### Schema-on-read

An approach where data structure is interpreted when data is read rather than enforced when it is written. *See [Ch 02](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch02-data-models.md).*

### Seat-based pricing

Charging per named user, which exposes software vendors when AI agents replace human users. *See [Ch 34](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch34-application-giants-data-platforms.md).*

### Secondary index

an index on a column other than the primary key that points back to the table's rows. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### Secondary sale

existing shareholders selling shares to new investors; the company receives no new money. *See [Ch 32](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch32-ai-native-data-companies.md).*

### Section-aware chunking

splitting along the headings, pages and tables recovered by a layout parser. *See [Ch 17](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch17-unstructured-data-processing.md).*

### Segment

In Apache Druid and Pinot, an immutable, time-partitioned, indexed columnar data file. *See [Ch 23](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch23-real-time-analytics-htap.md).*

### Self-correction loop

executing or dry-running generated SQL and feeding errors and sanity-check failures back to the model to repair the query. *See [Ch 22](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch22-agents-and-data.md).*

### Semantic cache

A cache that returns a stored LLM answer when a new prompt is close in meaning to an earlier one, matched by embedding similarity. *See [Ch 29](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch29-operational-database-vendors.md).*

### Semantic chunking

placing chunk boundaries where the embedding similarity between adjacent sentences drops. *See [Ch 17](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch17-unstructured-data-processing.md).*

### Semantic deduplication

removing documents with near-identical meaning, even when worded differently, by clustering their embeddings. *See [Ch 20](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch20-training-data-supply-chain.md).*

### Semantic layer

A shared set of business definitions of metrics and entities used consistently by BI tools and AI agents. *See [Ch 01](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch01-data-stack-map.md).*

### Semantic view

Snowflake's schema-level database object that stores a semantic model (metrics, dimensions, relationships). *See [Ch 14](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch14-semantic-layers-and-bi.md).*

### Sensor

An orchestrator task that waits for an external condition (file arrival, partition, event) before downstream work starts. *See [Ch 12](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch12-transformation-and-orchestration.md).*

### Separation of storage and compute

keeping durable data in shared (usually object) storage while stateless compute clusters scale independently. *See [Ch 05](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch05-analytical-engines.md).*

### Serverless compute

Vendor-managed, near-instantly available compute billed as one all-in price that includes the underlying cloud machines. *See [Ch 25](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch25-databricks.md).*

### Shadow data

copies of data that sit outside governed, catalogued systems, such as exports, snapshots and scratch buckets. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

### Sharding

splitting a dataset into partitions stored on different nodes so capacity scales out. *See [Ch 04](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch04-distributed-databases.md).*

### Share group

Kafka 4.x queue-style consumption (KIP-932) in which several consumers process records from the same partition with per-record acknowledgment. *See [Ch 11](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch11-streaming-and-event-platforms.md).*

### Shared-nothing

an architecture in which each node owns its own CPU, memory and disk and holds a partition of the data. *See [Ch 05](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch05-analytical-engines.md).*

### SharedMergeTree

ClickHouse Cloud's MergeTree variant that keeps all table data on shared object storage with stateless replicas. *See [Ch 23](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch23-real-time-analytics-htap.md).*

### Shuffle

redistributing rows across nodes by key so that related rows meet for a join or aggregation. *See [Ch 05](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch05-analytical-engines.md).*

### SIMD

single instruction, multiple data: one CPU instruction applied to many values held in a wide register. *See [Ch 05](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch05-analytical-engines.md).*

### Singer

an open specification for "taps" (sources) and "targets" (destinations) that exchange JSON records; the basis of Meltano. *See [Ch 10](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch10-ingestion-and-integration.md).*

### Slot

BigQuery's unit of query compute capacity, billed on reservations or consumed on demand. *See [Ch 28](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch28-hyperscaler-data-platforms.md).*

### Small data

The thesis that most analytical queries touch data small enough to process on one machine. *See [Ch 23](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch23-real-time-analytics-htap.md).*

### Small-files problem

the slowdown and overhead caused when a table accumulates many undersized data files, typically from frequent streaming commits. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Snapshot expiration

removing table snapshots older than a retention window so files they alone reference can be physically deleted. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Snapshot isolation

a guarantee that each reader sees one consistent committed version of the data, unaffected by writes in progress. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Snowflake CoWork

Snowflake's AI assistant for business users, renamed from Snowflake Intelligence at Summit 2026. *See [Ch 27](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch27-databricks-vs-snowflake.md).*

### Snowflake credit

Snowflake's unit of compute consumption, burned per hour by warehouse size and priced in dollars by edition and region. *See [Ch 27](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch27-databricks-vs-snowflake.md).*

### Snowflake Postgres

Snowflake's managed PostgreSQL service, built on the 2025 Crunchy Data acquisition and generally available from June 2026. *See [Ch 27](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch27-databricks-vs-snowflake.md).*

### Software-defined asset

Dagster's core abstraction: a data asset declared in code together with its upstream dependencies and how to compute it. *See [Ch 12](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch12-transformation-and-orchestration.md).*

### Source-available license

A licence that publishes source code but restricts its use, typically barring competing hosted services; not open source under the OSI definition. *See [Ch 29](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch29-operational-database-vendors.md).*

### Sovereign cloud

a cloud region operated under local jurisdiction, often by locally resident staff, to meet data-sovereignty rules. *See [Ch 24](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch24-data-meets-compute-and-storage.md).*

### Space amplification

the ratio of bytes stored on disk to bytes of live data. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### SPANN

Microsoft's cluster-based billion-scale vector index with centroids in memory and posting lists on disk. *See [Ch 18](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch18-embeddings-and-vector-search.md).*

### Sparse primary index

An index holding one entry per block of rows (not per row), small enough to stay in memory. *See [Ch 23](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch23-real-time-analytics-htap.md).*

### SPFresh

An update-friendly extension of SPANN that rebalances clusters in place; basis of turbopuffer's index. *See [Ch 18](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch18-embeddings-and-vector-search.md).*

<a id="spider-2-0"></a>
### Spider 2.0

a 2024–2025 text-to-SQL benchmark of 632 real enterprise workflow tasks on large cloud schemas, where top 2025 systems solved about 21%. *See [Ch 22](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch22-agents-and-data.md).*

### SSPL

MongoDB's Server Side Public License (2018), which requires anyone offering the software as a service to publish the source of their whole service stack. *See [Ch 29](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch29-operational-database-vendors.md).*

### SSTable

a sorted string table: an immutable, sorted on-disk file produced by an LSM-tree flush or compaction. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### Star-tree index

Apache Pinot's index that pre-aggregates metrics over chosen combinations of dimensions for predictable low latency. *See [Ch 23](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch23-real-time-analytics-htap.md).*

### State store

where a pipeline records its progress (cursor values, log offsets) so it can resume without gaps or duplicates. *See [Ch 10](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch10-ingestion-and-integration.md).*

### Static data masking

permanently replacing sensitive values in a copy of the data, typically for test or vendor use. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

### Stream processing

Continuous computation such as filters, joins and aggregations over unbounded event streams. *See [Ch 11](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch11-streaming-and-event-platforms.md).*

### Streaming database

A database that keeps SQL materialized views continuously up to date from incoming streams (e.g., RisingWave, Materialize). *See [Ch 11](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch11-streaming-and-event-platforms.md).*

### Supervised fine-tuning

Training a model on example prompts paired with ideal responses (SFT). *See [Ch 16](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch16-ai-data-lifecycle.md).*

### Support annuity

Recurring maintenance revenue earned on an installed base of perpetual licences, such as Oracle's database support. *See [Ch 29](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch29-operational-database-vendors.md).*

### Synthetic data

Training data generated by models rather than collected from people or the web. *See [Ch 16](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch16-ai-data-lifecycle.md).*

### System of intelligence

The layer that combines data across systems of record so analytics and AI agents can decide and act. *See [Ch 34](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch34-application-giants-data-platforms.md).*

### System of record

The application whose data is the authoritative version of a business fact, such as CRM for customers or ERP for invoices. *See [Ch 34](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch34-application-giants-data-platforms.md).*

## T

### Table metadata file

Iceberg's JSON root file holding a table's schemas, partition specs, properties and snapshot list; the catalog points to the current one. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Tableflow

A Confluent feature that materializes Kafka topics as Apache Iceberg (or Delta Lake) tables in object storage, removing a separate ETL job. *See [Ch 30](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch30-data-movement-streaming-companies.md).*

### Tag-based policy

an access or masking policy attached to a tag, so it applies automatically to every object carrying that tag. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

### Tail latency

The latency of the slowest requests (e.g., the 99th percentile, p99), which governs how responsive a system feels. *See [Ch 23](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch23-real-time-analytics-htap.md).*

### Take rate

the share of gross billings a marketplace or staffing-style vendor keeps after paying its contractors. *See [Ch 20](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch20-training-data-supply-chain.md).*

### Take-or-pay

A supply contract in which the buyer pays for a committed volume whether or not it takes delivery. *See [Ch 28](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch28-hyperscaler-data-platforms.md).*

### Take-private

A buyout, usually by private equity, that delists a public company so it can be restructured away from quarterly markets. *See [Ch 30](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch30-data-movement-streaming-companies.md).*

### Technical catalog

the on-path service that resolves a table name to its current metadata, arbitrates atomic commits and enforces access policy for every engine. *See [Ch 08](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch08-catalogs-and-metastores.md).*

### Tender offer

An offer to buy existing shares from employees and holders, often used by private companies to provide liquidity. *See [Ch 25](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch25-databricks.md).*

### Term license

A time-limited software licence (for example MongoDB Enterprise Advanced) whose licence portion is recognised as revenue upfront under ASC 606. *See [Ch 29](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch29-operational-database-vendors.md).*

### Text-to-SQL

an LLM translating a natural-language question directly into a SQL query. *See [Ch 14](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch14-semantic-layers-and-bi.md).*

### TFRecord

TensorFlow's sequential record-stream file format for training examples. *See [Ch 06](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch06-file-formats.md).*

### Tiered storage

Offloading older log segments from broker disks to object storage while keeping recent data local (Kafka KIP-405). *See [Ch 11](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch11-streaming-and-event-platforms.md).*

### Time travel

querying a table as it existed at an earlier snapshot, version or timestamp. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Time-series database

A database tuned for time-stamped, append-mostly measurements and window aggregations. *See [Ch 02](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch02-data-models.md).*

### Timestamp oracle

a central service that issues strictly increasing transaction timestamps, as in Percolator and TiDB's Placement Driver. *See [Ch 04](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch04-distributed-databases.md).*

### Token

The sub-word unit a language model reads and predicts; English text averages roughly four characters per token. *See [Ch 16](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch16-ai-data-lifecycle.md).*

### Tokenization

replacing a sensitive value with a surrogate token that can be mapped back only by a privileged service or key. *See [Ch 15](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch15-governance-security-privacy.md).*

### Tombstone

a marker written in an LSM-tree to record a deletion until compaction removes the key. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### Topic

A named stream in Kafka, made up of one or more partitions. *See [Ch 11](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch11-streaming-and-event-platforms.md).*

### Trace

A record of one AI or agent run: prompt, retrieved context, tool calls, outputs and outcome. *See [Ch 16](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch16-ai-data-lifecycle.md).*

### Training-serving skew

a mismatch between the feature values a model saw in training and those it receives in production. *See [Ch 21](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch21-ml-platforms-feature-stores-llmops.md).*

### Trigger-based CDC

Change data capture that uses database triggers to copy each change into a shadow table, at a cost to every write. *See [Ch 09](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch09-pipeline-patterns.md).*

### TrueTime

Google's clock API, backed by GPS and atomic clocks, that returns a bounded interval of possible current times. *See [Ch 04](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch04-distributed-databases.md).*

### Two-phase commit

an atomic-commit protocol in which a coordinator collects prepare votes and then issues commit, blocking if it fails mid-protocol. *See [Ch 04](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch04-distributed-databases.md).*

### Two-phase locking

a pessimistic concurrency protocol that acquires locks as needed and releases them only after commit. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

## U

### Undo log

storage holding prior images of changed rows, used for rollback and for reading older snapshots (Oracle, InnoDB). *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### UniForm

Delta Lake's Universal Format feature, which writes Iceberg (and Hudi) metadata alongside the Delta log so other engines can read one copy of data. *See [Ch 07](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch07-open-table-formats.md).*

### Unit test

a test of transformation logic against mock input rows, run in development or CI rather than on production data. *See [Ch 13](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch13-data-quality-observability-lineage.md).*

### Unity Catalog

Databricks' governance catalog for tables, files, models and functions, handling permissions, lineage, audit and credential vending. *See [Ch 25](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch25-databricks.md).*

### Unstructured data

content without a predefined schema, such as documents, email, images, audio and video. *See [Ch 17](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch17-unstructured-data-processing.md).*

### Upsert

An operation that inserts a row or, if a row with the same key exists, updates it. *See [Ch 23](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch23-real-time-analytics-htap.md).*

### User-facing analytics

Analytics embedded in a product and queried by its end users or customers rather than by internal analysts. *See [Ch 23](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch23-real-time-analytics-htap.md).*

## V

### Vacuum

PostgreSQL's background process that reclaims space from dead row versions. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### Valkey

The Linux Foundation's BSD-licensed fork of Redis 7.2.4, created in March 2024. *See [Ch 02](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch02-data-models.md).*

### Vamana

The single-layer graph-construction algorithm behind DiskANN, which keeps some long edges to shorten searches. *See [Ch 18](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch18-embeddings-and-vector-search.md).*

### Vector database

A database built primarily to store, index and query embeddings with metadata filters. *See [Ch 18](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch18-embeddings-and-vector-search.md).*

### Vector index

A data structure for fast approximate nearest-neighbor search over embeddings. *See [Ch 01](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch01-data-stack-map.md).*

### Vectorized execution

query processing that passes cache-sized batches of values between operators instead of one row at a time. *See [Ch 05](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch05-analytical-engines.md).*

### Verifiable reward

A reinforcement-learning reward computed by an automatic check, such as unit tests passing or a math answer matching. *See [Ch 16](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch16-ai-data-lifecycle.md).*

### Virtual data environment

SQLMesh's layer of views over versioned physical tables that lets dev and CI environments reuse unchanged production data. *See [Ch 12](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch12-transformation-and-orchestration.md).*

### Virtual warehouse

Snowflake's independently sized, stateless compute cluster that reads shared table data. *See [Ch 05](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch05-analytical-engines.md).*

### Vision-language model

a model that takes images and text as input, used to parse rendered page images directly into Markdown or JSON (VLM). *See [Ch 17](docs/03-ai-data-stack/ch17-unstructured-data-processing.md).*

### Vitess

The open-source MySQL sharding system built at YouTube, CNCF-graduated in 2019 and commercialised by PlanetScale. *See [Ch 29](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch29-operational-database-vendors.md).*

### Volcano iterator model

the classic tuple-at-a-time execution design in which each operator pulls one row from its child via next(). *See [Ch 05](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch05-analytical-engines.md).*

### Volcano model

row-at-a-time query execution in which each operator pulls rows from its child through a next() call. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### Vortex

A compressed columnar file, memory and IPC format created by SpiralDB and hosted since 2025 by the LF AI & Data Foundation. *See [Ch 06](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch06-file-formats.md).*

## W

### Watermark

A stream processor's running estimate that all events up to a given event time have arrived, used to decide when to emit window results. *See [Ch 09](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch09-pipeline-patterns.md).*

### WebDataset

A training-data format that packs samples into tar shards so reads stay sequential while shards are shuffled. *See [Ch 06](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch06-file-formats.md).*

### Wide-column store

A database of sparse rows grouped by partition key and sorted by clustering key, descended from Google Bigtable. *See [Ch 02](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch02-data-models.md).*

### Workflow Data Fabric

ServiceNow's data layer combining RaptorDB, zero-copy connectors and a catalog for its agents. *See [Ch 34](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch34-application-giants-data-platforms.md).*

### Workload

The pattern in which software reads and writes data (size, frequency, latency and concurrency of operations). *See [Ch 01](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch01-data-stack-map.md).*

### Write amplification

the ratio of bytes physically written to storage to bytes the application logically wrote. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### Write skew

an anomaly where two transactions read overlapping data, write different rows and together violate a rule neither violates alone. *See [Ch 03](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch03-database-internals.md).*

### Write-ahead log

A sequential log of changes made durable before a database confirms a transaction; used for crash recovery, replication and CDC. *See [Ch 01](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch01-data-stack-map.md).*

### Write-back

An agent or tool changing data in the source application, subject to that application's business rules and approvals. *See [Ch 34](docs/04-company-deep-dives/ch34-application-giants-data-platforms.md).*

## Z

### Zero-copy

Handing data between components by sharing the same memory buffers instead of copying or converting them. *See [Ch 06](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch06-file-formats.md).*

### Zero-copy data sharing

Granting another account or organization query access to data in place, without duplicating it. *See [Ch 09](docs/02-pipelines-and-governance/ch09-pipeline-patterns.md).*

### Zero-ETL

Vendor-managed replication from an operational database into an analytical system that hides the pipeline from the user. *See [Ch 01](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch01-data-stack-map.md).*

### Zone map

per-chunk min/max statistics an engine checks to skip data that cannot match a filter. *See [Ch 05](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch05-analytical-engines.md).*

### Zstandard

A general-purpose compression codec (zstd) that gives higher ratios than Snappy at similar decompression speed. *See [Ch 06](docs/01-data-systems-foundations/ch06-file-formats.md).*
